figure_caption: Overview of the few-item prediction protocol and the evaluated configuration. A binary source matrix is used to fit a latent model, choose k=100 items, and fit stacking weights on source pseudo-targets; a new model answers only the selected items, and a stacked estimator predicts its full-benchmark accuracy. Targets are either random held-out models or models stronger than every source.

panels.title: Few-item prediction protocol
panels.short_caption: Binary source matrix, k=100 selected items, target answers and stacked full-score prediction, for the two target regimes.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: a source-only fitting stage picks k=100 items and stacking weights from a binary source matrix; at prediction time a new target model answers only those k items and a stacked estimator outputs its full-benchmark accuracy, under two target regimes. Wide 21:9 canvas, flow strictly left-to-right, in three vertical zones: LEFT 'Data' zone, MIDDLE 'Fit on sources only' zone (a grouping container), RIGHT 'Predict target' zone (a grouping container).

NODES (ID: shape/role: label):
- N_src: data node, sharp box placeholder: [[mp:binary_matrix]] a small heatmap-style grid of 0/1 cells (rows = models, columns = items), purely qualitative, no axes numbers; with three tiny text tags: 'Models' along the left side, 'Items' along the top, and the node title 'Source matrix $$S$$'. Highest-importance element along with N_k and N_pred.
- N_regime_rand: small rounded tag/box, label 'Random targets'; sub-label 'Random 20% held out'.
- N_regime_strong: small rounded tag/box, label 'Strong targets'; sub-label 'Above every source'. Next to N_regime_rand, stacked vertically under N_src, inside a small group labelled 'Target regime'. Optionally a tiny [[mp:regime_strip]] qualitative strip: a horizontal ability axis (no numbers) with the many source dots on the left/lower part, one 'random' target dot inside the source range, and 'strong' target dots clearly to the right beyond all source dots. Keep it small.
- N_latent: rounded box (process, fitted, trainable), label 'Logistic latent model'; small symbol label 'rank $$r$$'.
- N_design: rounded box (process), label 'Fisher D-optimal item design'.
- N_k: sharp data box highlighting selected columns: [[mp:selected_columns]] the same style of 0/1 grid but with exactly a few columns highlighted/outlined as selected, accompanied by the text label 'Selected items, $$k{=}100$$'. Highest importance.
- N_pseudo: rounded box (process), label 'Source pseudo-targets'; sub-label 'Held-out source folds'.
- N_stack: rounded box (process, fitted), label 'Stacking weights'; sub-label 'Non-negative, source-validated'.
- N_target: icon node: [[pl:small model icon: a simple neural-network / robot-head glyph]] labelled 'New target model'.
- N_answers: sharp data box, a single-row strip of k small 0/1 cells aligned in width with N_k, label 'Target answers $$Y$$'.
- N_est: rounded box (process, uses fitted weights), label 'Stacked estimator'. Inside or directly attached as a small row of three tiny chips: 'Calibrated mean', 'Linear', 'Logistic' (the three stack members), joined by a $$\oplus$$ node with weights riding as small labels on the inbound edges ($$w_1$$, $$w_2$$, $$w_3$$). Do not draw any formula box.
- N_pred: result node, sharp box with a gauge/percent glyph (simple, drawn in drawio), label 'Predicted full-benchmark accuracy $$\hat{y}$$'. Highest importance.
- N_true: small dashed-outline box, label 'True accuracy $$y$$', placed beside/below N_pred, as the reference (not an input).

GROUPS: G_fit = container around N_latent, N_design, N_k, N_pseudo, N_stack with title 'Fit on sources only' and a small 'no target info' lock-style text tag 'Target-blind'. G_pred = container around N_target, N_answers, N_est, N_pred, N_true with title 'Predict target'.

EDGES (source -> target; solid = forward data flow, dashed = auxiliary):
1. N_src -> N_latent, solid, no label.
2. N_latent -> N_design, solid, label 'Abilities, loadings'.
3. N_design -> N_k, solid, label 'Choose $$k$$'.
4. N_src -> N_pseudo, solid, routed below the latent/design row, no label.
5. N_latent -> N_pseudo, solid, short, no label.
6. N_pseudo -> N_stack, solid, no label.
7. N_regime_rand -> N_pseudo, dashed, label 'Random folds'.
8. N_regime_strong -> N_pseudo, dashed, label 'Strongest-holdout folds'. (The two regime edges are a crossing/parallel pair: give them distinct colors.)
9. N_regime_rand -> N_target, dashed, no label; N_regime_strong -> N_target, dashed, label 'Regime label' riding on the bundled pair; these two represent the choice of which models act as targets.
10. N_k -> N_target, solid, label 'Reveal only these items' (crosses the G_fit/G_pred boundary).
11. N_target -> N_answers, solid, label 'Answers $$k$$ items'.
12. N_answers -> N_est, solid, no label.
13. N_latent -> N_est, solid (routed above), label 'Ability prior'.
14. N_stack -> N_est, solid, label 'Weights $$w$$'.
15. N_est -> N_pred, solid, no label.
16. N_true -> N_pred, dashed, label 'Compare' (evaluation only, both endpoints adjacent).

SPATIAL LAYOUT: left zone has N_src at top, N_regime group below it. Middle zone G_fit: top row N_latent -> N_design -> N_k left to right; bottom row N_pseudo -> N_stack left to right, directly beneath. Right zone G_pred: N_target at left-top, N_answers right of it, N_est below/right, N_pred at far right, N_true tucked under N_pred. Align N_k and N_answers on the same horizontal band so the 'same k items' relationship reads at a glance. Keep edge crossings minimal; the only deliberate boundary crossings are edges 9, 10, 13, 14.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: (1) N_src, N_k, N_pred; (2) N_regime pair, N_answers, N_est; (3) N_latent, N_design, N_pseudo, N_stack; (4) N_true, edge labels, group titles.

TEXT BUDGET (exact labels, names only, no sentences): 'Source matrix $$S$$', 'Models', 'Items', 'Target regime', 'Random targets', 'Random 20% held out', 'Strong targets', 'Above every source', 'Fit on sources only', 'Target-blind', 'Logistic latent model', 'rank $$r$$', 'Fisher D-optimal item design', 'Selected items, $$k{=}100$$', 'Source pseudo-targets', 'Held-out source folds', 'Stacking weights', 'Non-negative, source-validated', 'Predict target', 'New target model', 'Target answers $$Y$$', 'Stacked estimator', 'Calibrated mean', 'Linear', 'Logistic', '$$w_1$$', '$$w_2$$', '$$w_3$$', 'Predicted full-benchmark accuracy $$\hat{y}$$', 'True accuracy $$y$$', plus edge labels listed above ('Abilities, loadings', 'Choose $$k$$', 'Random folds', 'Strongest-holdout folds', 'Regime label', 'Reveal only these items', 'Answers $$k$$ items', 'Ability prior', 'Weights $$w$$', 'Compare'). No raw multi-term equations anywhere.
